{
  "findings": [

      "line": 96,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Import Prisma before updating Salesforce credentials",
      "body": "The new credential update references `prisma`, but this file never imports or declares it. Type-checking fails with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`; if type-checking is bypassed, a successful token refresh throws a ReferenceError before returning the Salesforce connection. Import the shared Prisma client."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 97,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Persist the parsed Google credentials, not the safeParse result",
      "body": "`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success: true, data: credentials }`, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credentials themselves. Passing this result directly to `prisma.credential.update` nests all token fields under `key.data`. This also happens with syncing disabled: after an ordinary refresh, subsequent calendar operations no longer find the expected root-level OAuth fields. Persist the result's `data` instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Define actual expiry fields instead of computed Zod object keys",
      "body": "Calling `toString()` on these Zod schemas produces the literal key `[object Object]`, not a wildcard property definition; the second computed property also overwrites the first. Because Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, a synced response containing `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, and `refresh_token` loses those fields. Zoom then computes a NaN expiry, and Office365 cannot update its expiry correctly. Define and preserve the actual supported response fields."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Normalize external refresh responses for the SDK-based callers",
      "body": "The sync branch returns a native fetch `Response`, but Google Calendar and both Zoho services still read `.data`, while HubSpot expects a decoded token object with `accessToken` and `expiresIn`. None of those callers reads the response body. Even a successful JSON response therefore produces undefined token fields or throws before the credentials can be refreshed. Establish a consistent return contract and adapt these callers to decode the external response."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 93,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Pass the credential owner's user ID to the sync endpoint",
      "body": "The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a user ID, but this call passes the credential row's primary key. The helper sends that value as `calcomUserId`, so a credential whose ID differs from its owner's ID requests another user's tokens or fails lookup. Any returned tokens are then saved to the current credential and used for its CRM operations. Carry the actual nullable `credential.userId` into this method."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 25,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Do not replace an existing native refresh token with a placeholder",
      "body": "The placeholder assignment also runs when credential syncing is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly allows a refresh response without a replacement `refresh_token`, and its caller merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. Such a response now overwrites the valid stored refresh token with the literal `refresh_token`, making the next refresh fail. Leave an omitted native refresh token unset so the caller can preserve the existing value."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Authenticate outbound credential-sync requests",
      "body": "This token-retrieval POST contains only a user ID and app slug; it attaches no secret, signature, or other authentication. A public sync endpoint accepting this protocol cannot distinguish Cal from another caller requesting the same user's bearer token, while an endpoint requiring the configured shared secret will reject these calls. Add authenticated server-to-server requests, for example using the configured secret header, rather than relying on enumerable identifiers."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 92,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Send Zoom's canonical app slug",
      "body": "The refresh request sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are installed with `appId: \"zoom\"`, and the webhook identifies apps by that canonical slug. A parent store looking up the synced Zoom integration by the supplied slug will not find it. Pass `zoom` rather than the integration directory/API route name."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 75,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint",
      "body": "The new Salesforce refresh always posts directly to Salesforce and never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`. Consequently, enabling sharing and setting `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` has no effect on Salesforce token retrieval: Cal still requires a locally usable refresh token and refreshes independently of the parent store. Externally managed credentials whose refresh token is retained by the parent cannot work through this path."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Handle the access-token-only sync response in Webex",
      "body": "After routing Webex refreshes to the external endpoint, the response is still validated with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token expiry. An endpoint following the helper's documented access-token/expiry-only response therefore always fails with `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned`. Add a sync-specific parsing and merge path that does not require the parent to disclose its refresh token."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 67,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Do not delete externally managed Lark credentials based on local refresh tokens",
      "body": "Before reaching the new sync request, `refreshAccessToken` still deletes the credential if its local refresh token is absent or expired. With external credential management, the parent can hold a valid rotated refresh token even when Cal's local copy is missing or stale. Cal then deletes a recoverable integration without consulting the source of truth. Keep the local refresh-token validation and deletion inside the native-provider fallback."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 78,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Clear the invalid flag when replacing invalidated credentials",
      "body": "The existing-credential branch updates only `key`. Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials `invalid: true` after unrecoverable authentication failures, so pushing fresh valid credentials through this webhook leaves the integration marked invalid despite returning success. Reset the invalid state when accepting a valid replacement so the parent store can reconnect an invalidated integration."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Make initial webhook delivery idempotent under concurrency",
      "body": "The lookup and creation are separate operations. Two simultaneous deliveries for the same user and app can both find no credential and then create separate rows. Later deliveries update only one row through `findFirst`, leaving duplicate integrations with stale credentials. Serialize creation for the same sync identity or introduce a database-enforced idempotency mechanism rather than relying on this check-then-create sequence."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Import Prisma before updating Salesforce credentials
findings.body: The new credential update references `prisma`, but this file never imports or declares it. Type-checking fails with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`; if type-checking is bypassed, a successful token refresh throws a ReferenceError before returning the Salesforce connection. Import the shared Prisma client.

findings.title: Persist the parsed Google credentials, not the safeParse result
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success: true, data: credentials }`, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credentials themselves. Passing this result directly to `prisma.credential.update` nests all token fields under `key.data`. This also happens with syncing disabled: after an ordinary refresh, subsequent calendar operations no longer find the expected root-level OAuth fields. Persist the result's `data` instead.

findings.title: Define actual expiry fields instead of computed Zod object keys
findings.body: Calling `toString()` on these Zod schemas produces the literal key `[object Object]`, not a wildcard property definition; the second computed property also overwrites the first. Because Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, a synced response containing `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, and `refresh_token` loses those fields. Zoom then computes a NaN expiry, and Office365 cannot update its expiry correctly. Define and preserve the actual supported response fields.

findings.title: Normalize external refresh responses for the SDK-based callers
findings.body: The sync branch returns a native fetch `Response`, but Google Calendar and both Zoho services still read `.data`, while HubSpot expects a decoded token object with `accessToken` and `expiresIn`. None of those callers reads the response body. Even a successful JSON response therefore produces undefined token fields or throws before the credentials can be refreshed. Establish a consistent return contract and adapt these callers to decode the external response.

Any returned tokens are then saved to the current credential and used for its CRM operations. Carry the actual nullable `credential.userId` into this method.

Such a response now overwrites the valid stored refresh token with the literal `refresh_token`, making the next refresh fail. Leave an omitted native refresh token unset so the caller can preserve the existing value.

Add authenticated server-to-server requests, for example using the configured secret header, rather than relying on enumerable identifiers.

findings.title: Send Zoom's canonical app slug
findings.body: The refresh request sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are installed with `appId: "zoom"`, and the webhook identifies apps by that canonical slug. findings.title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
findings.body: The new Salesforce refresh always posts directly to Salesforce and never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`. Consequently, enabling sharing and setting `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` has no effect on Salesforce token retrieval: Cal still requires a locally usable refresh token and refreshes independently of the parent store. Externally managed credentials whose refresh token is retained by the parent cannot work through this path.

Add a sync-specific parsing and merge path that does not require the parent to disclose its refresh token.
